summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 45.2% YoY to Rs.178.1 crore, with operational EBITDA margin at 28.6%; management reaffirms Rs.4,000 crore cumulative revenue for FY27-28.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs.178.1 crore, flat sequentially but down 45.2% YoY, which management attributed to order-inflow timing with most order book slated for FY27. Operational EBITDA was Rs.51 crore (28.6% margin), down about 900 bps QoQ and 1,390 bps YoY, driven by fixed-cost deleveraging, year-end incentives, warranty provision true-up, export post-supply costs and higher R&D. Consolidated order book stood at Rs.1,336 crore, of which about Rs.1,000 crore is expected to execute in FY27, mainly in Q2 and Q3. Management focused its prepared remarks on anti-drone (hard-kill) systems, simulators, and new products launched at Prayagraj, including the HyperStrike interceptor drone and Vrishabh UGV.

financial_highlights.change: Flat QoQ vs Rs.177.8 crore in Q3 FY26; down 45.2% YoY vs Rs.325 crore in Q4 FY25
Down ~900 bps QoQ and ~1,390 bps YoY
Down 29.4% vs Rs.973.6 crore in FY25
Standalone Rs.1,222.6 crore; ~Rs.1,000 crore to execute in FY27, balance Rs.326 crore is AMC
Improved 42 days from 161 days at 31 Dec 2025

segments.name: Standalone
segments.commentary: FY26 standalone revenue about Rs.423 crore and standalone order book Rs.1,222.6 crore at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (ARI, UTS and others)
segments.commentary: Subsidiaries contributed about Rs.260 crore of FY26 revenue: ARI about Rs.131 crore (PAT margin ~30.3%, full-year consolidation after end-FY25 acquisition), UTS the bulk of the rest (PAT margin ~26.5%), others about Rs.10 crore.

segments.name: Subsidiary order book
segments.commentary: ARI order book about Rs.75 crore and UTS about Rs.35 crore at 31 March 2026, versus opening Rs.90 crore (ARI) and Rs.110 crore (UTS).

guidance_outlook: Cumulative FY27 and FY28 revenue target of Rs.4,000 crore reaffirmed; management said it is comfortable with the figure.
Management expects order book to touch about Rs.3,000 crore at some point; cited FY28 revenue of about Rs.2,500 crore as a scenario.
FY27 UTS and ARI combined revenue guided at about Rs.365 crore; ARI margin 27-30%, UTS about 30-31%.
Long-term guidance of 35% operational EBITDA and 25% PAT margin intact; R&D spend to stay elevated as a structural cost.
Long-term working capital cycle guided at 140-150 days; elevated near term due to inventory build for FY27 deliveries.
Management expects a good order inflow in Q1 FY27, no later than Q2; arms and ammunition working capital needs from next year at the earliest.
HyperStrike interceptor drone production to start in FY27 with initial capacity of 5,000 per shift per month, scalable to 15,000; Vrishabh UGV commercial launch planned in FY27.
risks_watch: Q4 margin compression: five factors cited (fixed-cost deleveraging, incentives ~Rs.5 crore, warranty true-up Rs.3.1 crore, export post-supply costs Rs.2.7 crore, R&D up Rs.3.3 crore QoQ); R&D increase described as structural.
Revenue visibility depends on FY27 execution of ~Rs.1,000 crore order book and on converting the Rs.1,500-few thousand crore pipeline; management said the first-quarter order inflow is still awaited.
Risk of procurement shifting toward foreign vendors in the near term, raised by an analyst; management disagreed and cited indigenisation push.
Simulator orders delayed; timing of government simulator procurement remains uncertain.
Working capital days at 196 with inventory and supplier advances; a sustained elevated cycle would pressure cash generation.
Ammunition certification timeline (FY27 start) and arms licence revenue contribution beyond year two remain uncertain.
Acquisition plans in 'Pareto technologies' were mentioned without a specific target or timeline.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and expansive on the long-term product and demand narrative, but cautious and vague on near-term timing, with order-conversion and pipeline questions answered largely with qualitative statements. Financial commentary was measured and explanatory around the Q4 margin dip.
key_quotes: We stick to that prediction of our projection of Rs.4000 Crores turnover in FY2027 and 2028 put together, so, we are very comfortable with those figures now.
Unlike the other four factors mentioned earlier, which are largely one-time or period-specific in nature, this is a structural commitment that we will continue.
I think we have figure of factored exports also in this and we personally think that the simulator market is showing a lot of hope.
I think the margins will continue as long as we are actually providing a lot of value to the customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.1,336 crore order book converts into FY27 revenue, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs.1,000 crore of the order book is for FY27 dispatch, with the balance Rs.326 crore being AMC; most deliveries expected in Q2 and Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs.4,000 crore FY27-28 revenue target require about Rs.3,000 crore of orders in hand, and is that achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the cumulative Rs.4,000 crore target stands, with about Rs.2,500 crore in FY28 as a scenario, and said it is reasonable to expect the order book to touch Rs.3,000 crore at some point; no specific timing given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.4,000 crore projection exports-inclusive, and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the factored exports are included, with simulator demand (drone-related and naval) and anti-drone exports expected to be significant; no export order value quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the government procurement shift toward foreign vendors in the near term, and what is the risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman disagreed, saying the armed forces and government are aligned on indigenous procurement and that consolidation over three to five years will favour winners; no quantified response.

qa_highlights.question: Are any orders expected before Q3-Q4, and what is the bottleneck in simulator ordering?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the first quarter should be good and no later than Q2; simulator orders were delayed as government moved to emergency procurement of anti-drone systems during Operation Sindoor.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook as hardware share rises, and working capital needs for ammunition?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the 35% operational EBITDA and 25% PAT margin targets are intact for the next couple of years; CFO said working capital stays at 140-150 days long term, with 196 days now due to FY27 inventory build.

capex_capacity: HyperStrike interceptor drone: production to start in FY27; initial capacity about 5,000 per shift per month, scalable to 15,000 per month if demand rises (management)
Vrishabh UGV: commercial launch planned in FY27; indigenous content above 85%; payload 150 kg, speed 50 km/h, range up to 100 km (management)

Weapon systems (RCWS / 12.7, 20mm, 30mm gun integration): management said weapon systems to launch during FY27, with majority launched in the following year; arms and ammunition licences recently received
30mm smart ammunition: testing ongoing with certifying agency involved; manufacturing and supply expected next financial year, with a roughly two-year window to get everything in order

Working capital cycle: currently 196 days; long-term guidance 140-150 days; outsourcing-led assembler model retained, with only critical arms components to be made in-house; arms/ammunition working capital needs from next year at the earliest
Subsidiaries FY27 guidance: ARI and UTS combined revenue about Rs.365 crore; FY28 expectations cited for ARI about Rs.300 crore and UTS Rs.150-200 crore
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book Rs.1,336 crore at 31 March 2026, of which about Rs.1,000 crore expected to execute in FY27 (mostly Q2 and Q3) and balance Rs.326 crore is AMC spread over contract periods

Bidding pipeline cited at about Rs.1,500 crore, with single-vendor tenders and other tenders potentially adding a couple of thousand crore; overall pipeline 'running into a few thousands of crores'; split roughly 55:45 anti-drone to simulator
Management expects a good order inflow in Q1 FY27, no later than Q2; simulator orders delayed by government shifting to emergency procurement of anti-drone systems after Operation Sindoor
Hard-kill anti-drone orders received to date about Rs.40 crore, including L70 supplies and two more recent orders; repeat and upgrade orders post Operation Sindoor
Anti-drone demand: management said post Israel-Iran conflict focus has risen at least 2x versus original projection; impact on turnover not yet quantified
Pricing positioning: HyperStrike targeted at about $10,000 per unit versus Shahed drone at about $30,000; management says ZEN prices to be best value-for-money against mainly foreign competitors
Subsidiary order book: ARI about Rs.75 crore and UTS about Rs.35 crore at 31 March 2026, versus opening Rs.90 crore (ARI) and Rs.110 crore (UTS)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed Rs.4,000 crore cumulative FY27-28 revenue and guided UTS+ARI to about Rs.365 crore in FY27, backed by a Rs.1,336 crore consolidated order book (about Rs.1,000 crore to execute in FY27, mostly Q2-Q3), though Q4 revenue fell 45.2% YoY and the new products (HyperStrike, Vrishabh, weapons) are not yet producing and the Rs.4,000 crore target has no specific capacity behind it.
